messages.subject: Re: TsDyn
parts:
Dear Johan

I am glad the package was useful for you! I guess we will be happy to
have a look on your thesis, so please send a copy of it when finished!
And thanks in advance for citing the package!

Concerning your question, do you refer to the predict.nlar function? It
is actually Antonio di Narzo (cc) who wrote it, so he might better
answer your questions. In any case, you can access the code either by
downolading source code from CRAN or typing:
getAnywhere(predict.nlar)

Note that we have a mailing list: ts...@googlegroups.com
<mailto:ts...@googlegroups.com> rather inactive but useful to know abt
tsDyn improvements.

At your disposition for more precise questions

Matthieu

Johan Sjöberg a écrit :
> Hello Matthieu,
>
> I’m writing to you regarding the r-package tsDyn that I have – with
> great pleasure – been using to write my master thesis in mathematical
> statistics at stockholm university.
>
> I was wondering about the details of the simulation based predictions
> of SETAR and LSTAR models. I have found no details of the number of
> simulations and from which distribution the error term is drawn (even
> though I presume it’s normal. I would be very greatful if you could
> enlighten me.
>
> Thanks again for tsDyn, I will make sure to properly cite the package
> in the report .
>
> Best Regards
>
> Johan Sjöberg
